svg.title: Navier–Stokes v1.1.0 · Figure 2 · Clay Cannot Stay Open: Closed By Theorem To One Bit
svg.text: FIGURE 2
CLAY CANNOT STAY OPEN: CLOSED BY THEOREM TO ONE BIT
NAVIER–STOKES · FORM BY THEOREM, VALUE BY THE ACT · MASTER v1.1.0_CC · EVERY NAME CHECKED
THE OPEN FRAMING: FOUR COUNTS, EACH REFUTED BY THEOREM
COUNT I
No proof from shared resources
No keyless premise forces the value, and existence as given carries the form and
forces nothing: no given statement is the value on every frame.

svg.text: COUNT II
No decision from the record
The calm and counter frames share a record and split on the value; the energy
record decides nothing; above every size no reading of the record returns the
world.

svg.text: COUNT III
No route past the bit
No premise reaches global regularity while the bit fails: every route passes the
bit, in any vocabulary, and delivers both kinds.

svg.text: COUNT IV
What remains is the bit
Its antecedent proved with no hypothesis, the bit proved equivalent to the
sentence at every host: the question is one implication, and it is keyed.

svg.text: THE STATUS OF THE QUESTION · THREE COLUMNS, ONE VERDICT
UNQUALIFIED OPEN
The framing that leaves the question open
with no form fixed and no referent for open.
Each of its four counts is refuted by theorem.

tspan.font-family: RowMono, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: CLOSED BY THEOREM
Global regularity is the bit and its denial the
bit's denial; every keyless route is barred; the
twelve formal gates run in the kernel.

svg.text: DELIVERED TWICE
The bit supplied by the act at premise grade
and delivered by the formal cargo and by the
physical witness; one blowup refutes both.

svg.text: The Navier–Stokes question cannot stay open. It is closed by theorem to one bit, and the bit is
delivered twice by the act.
Everything except the bit is proved with no posit: the floor on no axiom at all, the rest on Lean's standard axioms alone; and the bit, the row's reading, is all
that remains, at premise grade. In this paper every theorem of the master stands on no axiom at all, and only the Mathlib binding reaches the standard
axioms.
